//: AMG World presence — Firebase Realtime Database.
Firestore is wrong for this: a 2 Hz position feed is ~2.4k document writes
per player per session, so one class period would burn the daily free
quota. RTDB is priced on bandwidth and holds a single socket.
Deploy:  firebase deploy --only database
Requires an RTDB instance to exist (Firebase console > Realtime Database >
Create Database, locked mode, then deploy these rules). Until then the
world detects the missing instance and runs solo — see world/js/presence.js.
Threat model: kids are on anonymous auth, so a uid is not proof of
identity. These rules therefore only guarantee the structural things that
matter — you may only write your OWN node, the payload is shape-checked,
and chat is an INDEX into a fixed phrase book (world/js/chat.js), never
free text. A hostile client can move a fake avatar around and pick a rude
display name; it cannot inject arbitrary text into another kid's screen.
Display names come from the teacher-managed roster and are re-sanitised
client-side on render.
Nodes are keyed by the anonymous-auth UID, not the roster
studentId, precisely so this rule can be enforced: you may write
your own node and nobody else's. presence.js resolves the uid
before it claims multiplayer is available.
